commitResults.messageTitle: Name change: ip requires the name to be changed for level 0
Add greeting: fulfil the level 0 requirements by adding a greeting and exits
Add Echo: fulfil Level-1 requirements by adding echo functionality

Add add, list and mark as done: This fulfils the requirements of Level-2 and Level-3. Adding two increments was an accident, but from the course website it was stated that I can simply add the necessary tags and splitting the increments was optional
add ToDos, Events, Deadlines: adding this fulfils the Level-4 requirement. Reformat many strings in Sunny and add string formatting to the three new classes

add exception and error handling: add this to fulfil Level-5 requirements. Create multiple classes to handle most errors and exceptions at this version. Add specific handling of errors and guides to the user in future commit
add delete: add this to fulfil Level-6 requirements Add this with some minor flaws in error catching and commenting

commitResults.messageBody:
Code cannot handle specific types of errors

This was caused by incorrect implementation of some code

Let's tweak the implementation of some code and add another exception
class to handle more exceptions that can occur

More specific error handling ensures the code does not break

Add save functionality and previous commit content.

Previous commit could not save task data into hard disk and did not contain changes previous message's data implied.

Code simply did not have such data.

Let's introduce the correct changes and functionality for saving.

Use file methods proposed on course website and conventional file
writing/reading tecniques.

Previous system saw dates and time as mere strings and lacked
functionality that actual dates and time would have.

Let's save dates and time as LocalDateTime objects from Java's library,
while also ensuring custom text that are obviously not dates be allowed
for user customizability.

This would provide such functionality that previously wasn't there,
while preserving user ability to use whatever they wish for dates.

Previous functionality was all in one class.

This made code difficult to read, test and prone to merge conflicts.

Let's separate functionality into classes where each is responsible for
their own requirements.

This will rectify the problems stated above.

Previous code has all files in one package/file.

This can cause longer loading times and unreadibility.

Let's separate all classes into packages determined by their
responsibility.

This rectifies the aforementioned problems.

Previous files were wrongly named packages having camelCase rather than all lowercase. Previous code also did not have gradle.

This would violate coding standards and quality, and lacked gadle support.

Let's rename the files and add gradle.

This will follow coding standards and allow building and running of gradle

Previous code must be manually tested.

This wastes time

Let's implement unit tests through JUnit.

This helps automate testing whenever changes are made.

The code contained no JavaDoc comments.

This can cause confusion and affect readability as nothing clarifies
what the code does.

Let's implement JavaDoc comments above each public and non-trivial
private methods and classes.

This improves readibility by clarifying what the code does.

Previous code did not follow the course's import order.

This would not follow coding standards.

Let's configure the import order in intellij and apply it to the entire
directory.

This ensures that the code's imports will follow coding standards. Rest
of code should be already following coding standards.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add functionality to find tasks using keywords
commitResults.messageBody:
Previous code provided no way to find specific tasks.

Users may have to manually find them through the taskboard list which is
prone to mistakes.

Let's implement a case in UserParser and a method in UI to find tasks
based on a keyword and print them out.

This will allow users to find tasks by inputting "find keyword" where
only 1 keyword is allowed.

Previous build was done purely on the terminal.

While retaining CLI requirements, user experience is severely affected.

Let's implement a GUI to improve user readibility.

This would improve user experience.
